evidence: tcpcl.lisp:617-618 `(let ((listener nil) (code +fnn-exit-ok+) (trace (fnn-tcl-trace-stream trace-path)) (spool-lock (fnn-tcl-spool-acquire spool))) (unwind-protect ...` with tcpcl.lisp:593-594 `(fnn-open path (logior sb-posix:o-wronly sb-posix:o-creat sb-posix:o-trunc))` (no O_NOFOLLOW). The same pattern is in fnn-command-tcpcl-send (653-654).
fix: Acquire the spool lock first, open the trace inside the unwind-protect, and open it with O_NOFOLLOW (and O_EXCL or a fresh name rather than O_TRUNC).
reviewer: tcpcl.lisp:617-618 and 653-654: in the parallel let, fnn-tcl-trace-stream (593-594, O_TRUNC) runs before fnn-tcl-spool-acquire. A second instance therefore truncates the live instance's trace before it is refused. That trace stream is outside the unwind-protect and is never closed, though the process exits right after the refusal, so the fd leak does not matter. The truncation does destroy the first run's replay evidence. Severity is low: this is the lab tcpcl verb, and it needs an operator to reuse the same TRACE path.
scenario: A second `tcpcl listen` with the same SPOOL and TRACE starts while the first is running. It O_TRUNCs the first instance's trace (the first keeps writing at its old offset, leaving a hole of zeros that fnn-tcl-trace-steps then rejects as a non-decimal field). Only then is it refused with `spool is already owned`, and the trace fd is never closed because the acquisition sits outside the unwind-protect. The replay differential evidence of the live run is destroyed.
title: tcpcl verbs truncate the trace file before taking spool ownership and leak its fd when ownership is refused
